issue.title: fix(release): verify final branch reference identity
issue.body:
Production release validation could skip the final live-source check when using executed qualification, and the shared branch guard compared only the extracted SHA. Validate the complete branch reference and require the late check in the protected release context while preserving offline local qualification and exact recorded CI run/attempt checks.

The five-file change preserves the newer final prepare hook, source-CI delegation, package qualification, publisher and prerelease controls. CI-proof test doubles remain mode-specific; a private omission mutation is refused.

Validation: 79 source-CI cases, 28 live-reference cases, four real wrapper scenarios, full pure publisher checks, 68 selected Python cases, legacy/v2 workflow assertions, a resource-free Release build with no warnings or errors, and the three controlled Aspire equality cases passed. The earlier 71-case artifact check is retained separately. Hosted source CI and genuine publication remain separate gates.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes core release publication guards and GitHub API trust boundaries; mistakes could block releases or weaken pre-publish source verification.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Release source checks are tightened** so publication cannot rely on a matching commit SHA alone or skip the final live verification when legacy **executed** qualification runs in production.
> 
> `verify-g4-release-source.sh` now validates the **entire** Git ref payload from the API (`ref`, canonical `url`, commit `object` type/SHA/urls), rejecting foreign repos, wrong refs, tags, or malformed JSON even when the digest happens to match.
> 
> `Assert-CurrentReleaseSource` still stays **offline** for local executed qualification, but when `GITHUB_JOB` is **release** it requires the full protected context (Builds repo, `main`/`prerelease`, `workflow_dispatch`, matching `build-release.yml` ref/SHA, valid run id/attempt), always runs the bash late guard, and only passes **EXPECTED_CI_RUN_*** env vars for **ci** mode—not for executed legacy releases.
> 
> Tests were expanded across the bash guard (malformed live refs), source-CI PowerShell (release-context executed path + foreign env rejection), and publisher fixtures (executed releases must invoke live guard once; CI proof expectations are mode-aware).
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 43adaa5d30437bec89f9485d414b1f92342b617c. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

issue.title: fix(deps): adopt the published EventStore SDK 4.1.0
issue.body:
Builds still selects EventStore 4.0.4. Select the published 4.1.0 cohort so the packaged host can consume the SDK app-channel fix, and bind its exact release and declaration identities. Extend the resolved Gateway receiver gate to exact 4.1.0 while preserving 4.0.4, alias refusals, and mapped-source boundaries.

Align the v1 schema and controlled fixture corpus with SDK 4.1.0 and recompute their dependent hashes while preserving the same refusal checks. Refresh only EventStore feed evidence from committed declarations; preserve the other 303 package rows, 155 family rows, and all prior observations. The audit requires declaration commit `82b4032afeca8a48b82678ff6673e757df1ff692` to remain an ancestor: use the already-authorized eligible owner exemption for a merge commit after green checks.

Validation:
- Full local Debug native reports: 2,815 module and 191 evidence passes, plus one offline integration pass. Four module platform/mapping exclusions and 12 live integration opt-ins remain unexecuted. All 98 exact earlier failure names now pass locally.
- Local packaged-tool qualification and required controls passed. Its record correctly remains publication-ineligible because source validation was explicitly skipped; the later normal release must perform full source qualification.
- Debug build and Release host build passed with zero warnings or errors. The actual resolved Gateway DLL matches the signed public 4.1.0 payload.
- Central, authoritative, and Platform catalog checks passed. The refreshed audit validator and both audit regression suites passed.
- Upstream [SDK 4.1.0](https://github.com/Hexalith/Hexalith.EventStore/releases/tag/v4.1.0): all 14 signed public payloads and both container architectures independently verified.

No new Memories publication or runtime admission is included. Platform adoption and Works full/CI qualification remain required.

issue.title: fix(runtime): bind released reference declarations
issue.body:
Package-mode composition cannot admit the catalog-selected EventStore 4.0.4, Tenants 6.0.0 and Memories 3.0.18 declaration snapshots because their release identities are absent from the default authority tables. Add the exact published release commits and declaration SHA-256 values, preserving every historical entry and all existing provenance checks.

The declarations were checked against the exact owner release sources: [EventStore 4.0.4](https://github.com/Hexalith/Hexalith.EventStore/blob/326bfef884543cdbcaf96de7f4c4ad378dbad6d7/module/hexalith.module-manifest.v2.json), [Tenants 6.0.0](https://github.com/Hexalith/Hexalith.Tenants/blob/9e5a991d0ba304bac7b1a5809cd71797b47d78ed/module/hexalith.module-manifest.v2.json), and [Memories 3.0.18](https://github.com/Hexalith/Hexalith.Memories/blob/66822bc5bc4858c824f17b7d093f5f0f676b03ea/module/hexalith.module-manifest.v2.json). Their official family archives have matching release-source metadata and valid NuGet signatures.

Validation:

- Fresh owning Tooling Debug build: zero warnings and errors.
- Four executable controls against the fresh production loader and exact released declaration/test-entry blobs pass: the known closure is admitted; changed source, coherently rehashed changed bytes, and an unqualified catalog version are refused.
- Exact commit and PR title pass pinned commitlint 21.2.4; diff whitespace check passes.

This change qualifies declaration bindings only. It allocates no services and activates no reference caller. Memories 3.0.18 image-source binding and combined runtime compatibility remain unqualified, and Platform snapshot adoption, tool release/adoption and hosted lifecycle acceptance remain separate gates.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Additive pinned metadata only; incorrect hashes would fail admission rather than silently change runtime behavior, and existing release bindings are unchanged.
> 
> **Overview**
> Package-mode composition was rejecting catalog-selected **EventStore 4.0.4**, **Tenants 6.0.0**, and **Memories 3.0.18** because those release identities were missing from the default authority tables in `CompositionDeclarationOptions`.
> 
> This PR **extends** `DefaultReleaseCommits` with the published owner release SHAs and **extends** `DefaultReleaseSnapshotHashes` with the matching v2 declaration SHA-256 values, without removing or altering existing entries. `CompositionDeclarationClosure` can now admit those snapshots when it looks up `owner/version` during provenance checks.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 62d2cec88c384b9d80cdefc23f3fb330c848cad1. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

issue.title: fix(runtime): resolve the direct module catalog
issue.body:
Package-mode native CI in a module checkout with only direct dependencies fails before allocation: declaration loading looks for the Builds catalog inside Platform's uninitialized nested checkout. Select the module root's direct catalog when its resolved Platform identity identifies a consuming module. The existing resolver still verifies the module/Platform catalog pin, checkout and clean state; Platform-root callers and existing defaults retain their catalog path. Public signatures, release authorities, snapshots, budgets and cleanup behavior are unchanged.

Add real Git workspace regressions that resolve the mapping before cold declaration loading, with authentic released EventStore and Memories fixtures checked against production release hashes. No release-authority override dictionary or nested module initialization is used. Cover the direct-only layout, Platform root, dirty/missing/wrong catalog and dirty Platform refusals, changed snapshot hash and unknown release version.

Validation:
- Fresh owning Release build: zero warnings/errors.
- 83 focused tests pass with zero failures/skips: 8 direct-layout/default-authority cases, 23 declaration-closure cases, 9 released-metadata cases and 43 identity cases.
- Before the fix, the new lane records 6 passes/2 failures, reproducing the missing nested catalog; the published 4.43.4 public caller also reproduces HXP020 on the actual unchanged Parties checkout.
- Fresh signed pinned 4.43.4 preparation followed by LoadVerified and the source-built default declaration boundary loads EventStore, Tenants, Memories and Parties from the actual root-only layout before composition workspace materialization. Loaded Tooling bytes match the test/CLI/project outputs. This is metadata-only source diagnostic evidence.
- An additional source-built public execution diagnostic remains unqualified: it returns HXT007 with Aspire deliberately absent and creates no state/workspace. A standalone source Tooling 1.0.0 probe correctly refuses the genuine Platform tool range; that gate is unchanged. Both first results are retained.
- Exact commit/title and fixture commit text pass locked commitlint 21.2.4 under Node 24.22.1/npm 11.19.1.

Normal hosted checks, fresh qualified publication, official package content verification and coherent consumer adoption remain required. No published runtime, lifecycle cleanup or candidate acceptance is claimed. The existing source89 publication and Parties PR59 baseline are preserved.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes where composition reads package versions before workspace allocation; scope is narrow (consuming-module layout) but affects CI/runtime catalog authority for module checkouts.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **package-mode cold start** when a consuming module checkout has only direct `Hexalith.Builds` / `Hexalith.Platform` refs: declaration loading no longer looks for `Directory.Packages.props` under Platform’s **uninitialized nested** `references/Hexalith.Builds`.
> 
> In `CompositionDeclarationOptions.ReadCatalogVersion`, when `PlatformIdentity.IsPlatformRepository` is false, the catalog path is rooted at **`Mapping.Root`** instead of **`PlatformRoot`**; Platform-root callers and materialized workspace snapshot behavior are unchanged.
> 
> Adds **`DirectCatalogDeclarationTests`** with real Git fixtures: verified declaration closure without nested catalogs or `source-mapping`, module vs Platform manifest entry points, fail-closed resolver rules (HXW009/HXW011) for dirty/missing/wrong catalog and dirty Platform, and post-resolve refusal for tampered provenance or unknown catalog versions. Supporting **eventstore 4.0.4** and **memories 3.0.18** platform declaration fixtures back the released-hash checks.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 8b99302b592acaa49937bf3f714317378c5c1d09. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

The follow-up fixture extraction keeps the original production change and all inputs/assertions unchanged. Released declaration writing now has its own cohesive helper; the setup/helper methods are 35/24 raw lines. Fresh owning Release build passes with zero warnings/errors and all eight affected direct-layout cases pass with zero failures/skips. The original 83-case evidence remains bound to its original head; normal current-head hosted gates remain required.

issue.title: fix(deps): adopt the published EventStore SDK 4.1.0
issue.body:
Builds still selects EventStore 4.0.4. Select the published 4.1.0 cohort so the packaged host can consume the SDK app-channel fix, and bind its exact release and declaration identities. Extend the resolved Gateway receiver gate to exact 4.1.0 while preserving 4.0.4, alias refusals, and mapped-source boundaries.

Align the v1 schema and controlled fixture corpus with SDK 4.1.0 and recompute their dependent hashes while preserving the same refusal checks. Refresh only EventStore feed evidence from committed declarations; preserve the other 303 package rows, 155 family rows, and all prior observations. The audit requires declaration commit `82b4032afeca8a48b82678ff6673e757df1ff692` to remain an ancestor: use the already-authorized eligible owner exemption for a merge commit after green checks.

Validation:
- Full local Debug native reports: 2,815 module and 191 evidence passes, plus one offline integration pass. Four module platform/mapping exclusions and 12 live integration opt-ins remain unexecuted. All 98 exact earlier failure names now pass locally.
- Local packaged-tool qualification and required controls passed. Its record correctly remains publication-ineligible because source validation was explicitly skipped; the later normal release must perform full source qualification.
- Debug build and Release host build passed with zero warnings or errors. The actual resolved Gateway DLL matches the signed public 4.1.0 payload.
- Central, authoritative, and Platform catalog checks passed. The refreshed audit validator and both audit regression suites passed.
- Upstream [SDK 4.1.0](https://github.com/Hexalith/Hexalith.EventStore/releases/tag/v4.1.0): all 14 signed public payloads and both container architectures independently verified.

No new Memories publication or runtime admission is included. Platform adoption and Works full/CI qualification remain required.

response.title: fix(release): verify final branch reference identity
response.body:
Production release validation could skip the final live-source check when using executed qualification, and the shared branch guard compared only the extracted SHA. Validate the complete branch reference and require the late check in the protected release context while preserving offline local qualification and exact recorded CI run/attempt checks.

The five-file change preserves the newer final prepare hook, source-CI delegation, package qualification, publisher and prerelease controls. CI-proof test doubles remain mode-specific; a private omission mutation is refused.

Validation: 79 source-CI cases, 28 live-reference cases, four real wrapper scenarios, full pure publisher checks, 68 selected Python cases, legacy/v2 workflow assertions, a resource-free Release build with no warnings or errors, and the three controlled Aspire equality cases passed. The earlier 71-case artifact check is retained separately. Hosted source CI and genuine publication remain separate gates.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes core release publication guards and GitHub API trust boundaries; mistakes could block releases or weaken pre-publish source verification.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Release source checks are tightened** so publication cannot rely on a matching commit SHA alone or skip the final live verification when legacy **executed** qualification runs in production.
> 
> `verify-g4-release-source.sh` now validates the **entire** Git ref payload from the API (`ref`, canonical `url`, commit `object` type/SHA/urls), rejecting foreign repos, wrong refs, tags, or malformed JSON even when the digest happens to match.
> 
> `Assert-CurrentReleaseSource` still stays **offline** for local executed qualification, but when `GITHUB_JOB` is **release** it requires the full protected context (Builds repo, `main`/`prerelease`, `workflow_dispatch`, matching `build-release.yml` ref/SHA, valid run id/attempt), always runs the bash late guard, and only passes **EXPECTED_CI_RUN_*** env vars for **ci** mode—not for executed legacy releases.
> 
> Tests were expanded across the bash guard (malformed live refs), source-CI PowerShell (release-context executed path + foreign env rejection), and publisher fixtures (executed releases must invoke live guard once; CI proof expectations are mode-aware).
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 43adaa5d30437bec89f9485d414b1f92342b617c. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
